Our technology mirrors our people - Smart, Innovative & Forward Thinking www.geidea.net To maintain competitive advantage as we grow, we are currently looking for a new Senior Accountant – Revenue & Accounts Receivable Job purpose: Ensures all revenue earned by the UAE business from merchant payment acceptance is recognised accurately, billed correctly and collected, and that settlement accounts are reconciled. Without this role revenue could be misstated or lost, receivables would age into bad debt, and settlement differences would go undetected. Responsibilities: Revenue recognition: Records all revenue streams – merchant service fees, transaction fees, terminal rental, online gateway fees and value-added services – in line with IFRS 15. Revenue-related costs: Accounts for interchange, card network and processor fees netted against revenue. Settlement reconciliation: Reconciles transaction data, card network settlement reports, bank statements and the general ledger, and clears differences. Collections tracking and receivables management: Tracks collections and ensures accurate and timely application of cash receipts and settlement deductions against customer accounts in SAP. Prepares and analyses the receivables ageing report, follows up overdue balances with Sales, Account Management and Collection teams, and escalates high-risk accounts. Issues customer statements and balance confirmations, and resolves billing disputes and credit note requests within agreed timelines. Credit loss provisioning: Calculates the expected credit loss on merchant receivables under IFRS 9 and proposes write-offs. Month-end close and revenue reporting: Delivers all revenue and receivables closing entries, accruals and deferrals within close deadlines, and reconciles the receivables sub-ledger to the general ledger and to bank and settlement accounts. Prepares revenue analysis by product, channel and merchant segment – distinguishing gross processing volume from net revenue – with explanations of volume, price and mix variances against budget and prior periods, under IFRS (group) and applicable UAE statutory requirements. Controls, VAT and audit: Checks system pricing against merchant contracts to prevent revenue leakage, applies VAT to fee income and supports audits. Qualifications: Years of experience: 4–6 years in revenue accounting or accounts receivable, preferably in merchant acquiring, payments, fintech or banking (Must). Degree required: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance (Must); a professional qualification such as ACCA, CPA or CMA (Preferred). Functional Knowledge: IFRS 15 and IFRS 9, reconciliation of high transaction volumes, UAE VAT on services and advanced Excel (Must). SAP System Knowledge: Hands-on experience with SAP receivables, billing and revenue accounting (Must). Language: Fluent English, both written and spoken, is essential (Must). Business Expertise: Economics of card acceptance – merchant service fees, interchange, card network fees, chargebacks and settlement cycles (Must).
